Account summary: Accelerant EdgeWorks is an enterprise adtech platform that evaluates Redwood to replace parts of an internal Triton-based inference fabric. Primary driver: reduce per-impression model costs and improve tail latency during auctions.

Key technical targets and ask list: 
- Workload: ~1–3k QPS steady per traf cluster for reranking (128 tokens avg), intra-second decision window.
- Latency targets: p95 <= 75ms for reranking; p99 goal <= 150ms for critical auction path.
- Throughput expectations: target ~1k QPS sustained per model instance with batching engaged; want guidance on batching windows vs SLO tradeoffs.
- Cost sensitivity: looking to drop model serving cost 30–50% vs current mixed 16-bit Triton fleet. Interested in 4-bit quantization guidance (stable quality + perf).
- Caching: strong interest in prefix/KV cache across sessions (campaign-level prefixes), plus TTL hints for cold starts. Asked: can Redwood shard KV cache across GPUs and warm on deploy?
- Routing/fallback: must be able to route to cheaper quantized variants under load and failover to a smaller model if latency SLOs breach.
- Benchmarking: customer requested a reproducible perf sweep (g5 vs h100) including token-per-ms metrics, batching curves, and memory/KV behavior. They want the exact commands/containers used so they can reproduce on prem.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 required, SSO/SAML integration mandatory, KMS for key wrap, and EU residency for EU campaigns.

- "If p95 slips past 100ms during peak auctions we lose margin — need predictable degradation." — Head of Infra.
- "Show us a 48hr benchmark with our 3 sample workloads and the ability to reproduce locally." — CTO.
